beliefs: f splits the input on whitespace runs, reverses each segment, and joins with single spaces [E1-E6]
Case and punctuation are preserved and reversed with their segment [E1, E2]
Leading/trailing whitespace is dropped and internal runs become single spaces [E3, E4]
The last output segment gets one extra copy of its own first character prepended (the original last segment's last character, duplicated at the start of the reversed last segment) [E5-E8]
The extra character is suppressed when the input has trailing whitespace, but NOT when it has only leading whitespace [E9, E10]
notes: E10 shows leading whitespace alone does NOT suppress the doubling ('  ab'->'bba', ' x y'->'x yy'), while trailing whitespace does ('ab  '->'ba', 'a b  '->'a b'). So the condition is: duplicate only if the raw input has no trailing whitespace (leading whitespace is fine).
